title: Hi-res 3D (rig H2 at 8x) → pixelize + fix, as a replacement for the illustration-based masters
question: Does rendering the calibrated 3D rig at 8x (1024 px per 128 cell), then downscaling (E2 k-centroid / area / pixel-art-fixer / PixelOE / material vote) and fixing (rig-material palette lock, outline, orphans, head stamp), give better 96 px pixel art than the m96 masters?
method: Blender 5.2: mrender.py (rig H2 + springs) exec'd with an 8x resolution and extra lum/normal/depth passes. Styles: shade (existing toon), cel (locked-palette 3-band ramps from smoothed lum), celo (cel + hi-res depth/material lines), flat matid. 5 downscalers × 4 styles, each also with the m96 head stamp. Scored with metrics.py against the illustration and directly against the master. Scripts in exp/2026-10-28_sw_hires3d/scripts.
result: Every 3D candidate loses to the master in every view. SE ssim_b .38–.39 vs .67, sil .62 vs .83. E .64–.68 vs .76. S .75 vs .85. Downscaler choice moves ssim_b by ≤ .03 and style by ≤ .05. Without the head stamp the face is unusable (face_ssim ≤ .2). Best still: celo_kc_hs (Opus 4.5) or matv_hs (Argon 3.5); master = 7.
verdict: Rejected for stills. The gap is structural (T-pose sleeves, thin or missing obi, bell skirt with a bare thigh band, waist cinch, placeholder face), so no downscaler can close it. PixelOE and pixel-art-fixer add nothing over k-centroid on a known grid. See the hires3d motion entry for the animation side.
